assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks transformed precision timekeeping and opened new tests of fundamental physics and relativistic effects. Their precision and scientific reach make this a strong Nobel-level achievement.
assessment.attribution: Katori and Ye made complementary, independently influential contributions to the lattice-clock approach and its experimental realization.
assessment.maturity: Decades of progressively improved performance, independent implementations, and applications establish a mature field.
uncertainties: The clock advances are a broad international effort, so the boundary of credit beyond these two leaders merits care.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry made matter-wave phase measurement a powerful tool for precision tests of gravity, inertial sensing, and fundamental physics.
assessment.attribution: These researchers represent foundational interferometer concepts and experimental development across complementary generations of the field.
assessment.maturity: The method has been repeatedly demonstrated and refined, with a substantial record of scientific use; further deployment in space and field settings remains developing.
uncertainties: The candidate combines several applications and contributions, making a single prize citation and precise credit boundary difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Interfaces that coherently connect light and matter enabled quantum memories and network nodes, opening a major experimental direction in quantum information.
assessment.attribution: Rempe, Kimble, and Lukin led distinctive approaches to cavity interfaces, atom-photon coupling, and memory and network concepts.
assessment.maturity: Core operations are well demonstrated, though large, reliable quantum networks remain an active engineering and physics challenge.
uncertainties: The field has many important contributors, and the credited work spans related but not identical platforms.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light overcame a fundamental measurement-noise limit in interferometry and now improves gravitational-wave detection, a clear connection between quantum optics and observation of the universe.
assessment.attribution: Caves established the theoretical measurement framework, Kimble advanced optical squeezing experiments, and Mavalvala helped bring squeezed-light methods into gravitational-wave observatories.
assessment.maturity: The technique is experimentally established and in operational use, with continued refinement across observatories.
uncertainties: Roman Schnabel and other experimental teams have made major contributions to detector-ready squeezed light, complicating a three-person attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Baryon acoustic oscillations provide a robust standard ruler for measuring cosmic expansion and have become a central probe of cosmology.
assessment.attribution: These names capture influential theory and landmark survey analyses, though the result depended on broad teams and successive generations of surveys.
assessment.maturity: The signal has been measured across large surveys and redshifts, with independent confirmation and continuing cosmological use.
uncertainties: The credited list may not fully represent the distributed theoretical and observational work behind the method.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction and fault tolerance showed how fragile quantum information can, in principle, support scalable computation, profoundly shaping quantum information physics.
assessment.attribution: Kitaev, Steane, and Shor developed foundational, complementary approaches to quantum codes and fault-tolerant computation.
assessment.maturity: The theory is foundational and experimental demonstrations have advanced substantially, but large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computation is not yet established.
uncertainties: The scope joins several major theoretical ideas, and the eventual experimental impact remains uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Trapping and precision measurement of antimatter enable unusually direct tests of fundamental symmetries and gravity, and have created a sustained experimental program.
assessment.attribution: Gabrielse and Hangst led distinct, complementary approaches to precision studies of antiprotons and antihydrogen.
assessment.maturity: Antihydrogen production and increasingly precise measurements are established, though the most discriminating symmetry tests are still improving.
uncertainties: No decisive departure from established particle physics has emerged, and the discovery claim is less singular than a new effect.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Event Horizon Telescope imaging achieved horizon-scale observations of black holes and demonstrated a remarkable new capability in radio astronomy.
assessment.attribution: Falcke helped frame the imaging target, Doeleman led the observational effort, and Moran contributed foundational very-long-baseline interferometry work.
assessment.maturity: The initial image has been followed by independent imaging of another black hole and additional analyses, although the observational record remains comparatively young.
uncertainties: The result depends on a very large collaboration, making individual attribution difficult.
The direct images test strong-gravity predictions but do not yet resolve all questions about black-hole physics.
